Hi @lukasmasuch This feature looks promising, and I'm excited to see the progress being made! However after upgrading Streamlit to v1.57.0, I encountered an issue with my Streamlit setup under bazel. Bazel replicates the directory structure during the build process by creating a real folder tree but symlinking every individual file to its actual location in the cache to save disk space. This behavior applies to the static frontend files bundled with the Streamlit library. Here is an example of the directory structure generated by Bazel: ```bash # The 'static' folder is real, but files inside are symlinks $ ll ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/ Permissions Size Date Modified Name ... lrwxr-xr-x@ - 21 Apr 15:39 file_util.py -> ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/file_util.py drwxr-xr-x@ - 21 Apr 15:39 static $ ll ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/static/ Permissions Size Date Modified Name lrwxr-xr-x@ - 7 May 15:59 favicon.png -> ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/static/favicon.png lrwxr-xr-x@ - 7 May 15:59 index.html -> ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/static/index.html lrwxr-xr-x@ - 7 May 15:59 manifest.json -> ~/.cache/bazel/.../site-packages/streamlit/static/manifest.json drwxr-xr-x@ - 7 May 15:59 static ``` ## The Problem The Starlette router used for serving Streamlit’s static files returns a 404 error because the default configuration for Starlette’s `StaticFiles` does not follow symlinks. Since the actual files reside outside the perceived "root" directory in the Bazel sandbox, Starlette blocks access to them for security reasons. ## Proposed Solutions After looking into the codebase, I believe there are two viable options to resolve this. (Details at the bottom.) ### 1. Set `follow_symlink = True` for `_StreamlitStaticFiles` `_StreamlitStaticFiles` inherits from `starlette.staticfiles.StaticFiles`. We can explicitly set the `follow_symlink` parameter to `True` in the constructor. Location: ```python # Proposed change super().__init__(directory=directory, html=True, follow_symlink=True) ``` This may have security implications as it allows serving files outside of the specified directory if there are symlinks pointing to them. However, since the static files are bundled with the Streamlit library and nothing else, this should not be a concern in this case. ### 2. Resolve the Static Files Path in `get_static_dir()` Streamlit's static directory path is determined by `get_static_dir()` function which is calculated relative to `file_util.py` location. Since `file_util.py` is also a symlink in the Bazel environment, we can resolve the physical path using `os.path.realpath` before passing it to the handler. Location: ```python def get_static_dir() -> str: """Get the folder where static HTML/JS/CSS files live.""" dirname = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(__file__)) # `realpath` instead of `normpath` return os.path.normpath(os.path.join(dirname, "static")) ``` Note: The result of this function is passed to `create_streamlit_static_handler` as `directory=`. I understand that Bazel support might not be a primary focus for the project, but addressing this would significantly improve compatibility for users in monorepo and containerized environments. Thank you for taking the time to read through this long report. I wanted to provide as much context as possible to make it easier to evaluate.

Commenting out both would result in 404 but if I enable one of the options, streamlit behaves as expected. ```python import os from pathlib import Path import streamlit as st from starlette.staticfiles import StaticFiles from streamlit import file_util from streamlit.web.server.starlette import starlette_static_routes PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.resolve() ### 1. Set `follow_symlink = True` for `_StreamlitStaticFiles` create_static_handler = starlette_static_routes.create_streamlit_static_handler def monkeypatch_create_static_handler(directory: str, base_url: str | None) -> StaticFiles: """Wrapper.""" print(f"Creating static handler for directory: {directory}, base_url: {base_url}") result = create_static_handler(directory, base_url) result.follow_symlink = True return result starlette_static_routes.create_streamlit_static_handler = monkeypatch_create_static_handler ### 2. Resolve the Static Files Path in `get_static_dir()` get_static_dir = file_util.get_static_dir def monkeypatch_get_static_dir() -> str: """Wrapper.""" dirname = os.path.dirname(os.path.realpath(os.path.normpath(file_util.__file__))) return os.path.normpath(os.path.join(dirname, "static")) file_util.get_static_dir = monkeypatch_get_static_dir app = st.App( PROJECT_ROOT / "main.py", debug=True, ) ```

### Analysis

This is an **accessibility (a11y) bug** affecting `st.selectbox`. The reporter's "Tools Menu combo box" is a standard `st.selectbox` (confirmed by decoding the playground repro, which calls `st.selectbox("Tools menu", [...10 options...])`). When the dropdown is open, Windows screen readers announce only the option label and not the list position/count (e.g. "GWAC Baseline Consumption Plan, 1 of 10"), so users can't tell how many options exist or where they are in the list.

**Potential root cause:** `st.selectbox` was recently migrated from BaseWeb to `react-aria-components` (`ComboBox` + `ListBox`/`ListBoxItem`, see `frontend/lib/src/components/shared/Dropdown/Selectbox.tsx`, PR #15438). The options are rendered as `role="option"` inside a `role="listbox"` that lives in a Floating UI portal, and the input uses the combobox + `aria-activedescendant` pattern. With that pattern, real focus stays on the input, so Windows screen readers (Narrator/JAWS/NVDA) rely on explicit `aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset` on each option to announce "X of Y". The Streamlit source does not set these attributes (no `aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset` references in `frontend/lib/src`), and they are not emitted for a fully-rendered (non-virtualized) RAC list — which matches the reported symptom of the count/position being omitted. Note the issue was filed against 1.40.1 (BaseWeb era) but the linked playground runs current code, so the gap is present in the new implementation too. A maintainer should verify against a live screen reader.

## Update

We added `st.App(...).run()`in Streamlit 1.59. This doesn't add direct support for modules in `streamlit run`, but can be used to enable execution of modules via `python -m myapp`.

This gives Streamlit apps an officially supported Python entry point, so launcher files can be run directly with:

```bash
python app.py
uv run app.py
```

It also works well with PEP 723 inline script dependencies, e.g. a launcher can declare `streamlit` and app-specific dependencies directly in the file and be run with `uv run app.py` without a separate environment setup step.

Example:

```python
import streamlit as st

app = st.App("streamlit_app.py")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()
```

This is a feature request to prevent `st.chat_input` (and `st.file_uploader`) from submitting when an attached file is over the size limit, failed to upload, or has a format mismatch — and to optionally expose per-file upload status so developers can gate submission themselves.

Looking at the frontend (`frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/ChatInput/ChatInput.tsx`), the current behavior partially matches the report:
- **In-progress uploads are already gated:** the `dirty` memo returns `false` while any file has `status.type === "uploading"`, so the submit button is disabled during active uploads.
- **Errored files are the real gap:** files with `status.type === "error"` (oversized, wrong type, or failed upload) do **not** block submission — the submit button's `disabled` condition is `!dirty || disabled || isDisabledDuringRun || audioUploading`, which never inspects error status. Meanwhile `createChatInputWidgetFilesValue` filters to only `"uploaded"` files, so errored files are silently dropped from `ChatInputValue.files`. This is exactly the reported problem: the user can send a message believing all files attached, but the failed one is invisible to the app.

So implementing this would mean (a) extending the submit-disabled logic to also block while any file is in an `error` state, and (b) optionally surfacing per-file status to Python so apps can drive `disabled=` themselves. This is an enhancement rather than a bug.

### Related Issues

- [#11092](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11092) — "st.chat_input uploading unsupported files does not prevent sending message". Near-duplicate for the file-format-mismatch case; requests the same "block submission until invalid files are removed" behavior.
- [#12692](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12692) — "Add max_size parameter to each st.file_uploader to restrict file size before upload". This is the `max_upload_size` feature this issue explicitly builds on and whose silent-drop behavior it wants to address.
- [#12579](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12579) — "Separate maxUploadSize configuration for st.chat_input and st.file_uploader". Related work on per-widget upload size limits for chat input / file uploader.

This is a **feature enhancement** request for `st.spinner`. Today `st.spinner` is only available as a context manager (`with st.spinner(...):`), which ties the spinner's lifetime to a code block. The author wants a stand-alone spinner *element* that can be placed into a container/placeholder (e.g. `placeholder = st.empty(); placeholder.spinner("Loading…")`) and cleared later by writing something else into that same placeholder. The motivating use case is showing a loading indicator while data is being computed asynchronously, and it's called out as a blocker for the author's proposed non-blocking background-execution pattern (#6687). Suggested labels: `type:enhancement`, `feature:st.spinner`, `feature:st.empty`, `area:elements`.

This is a confirmed bug involving the interaction between `st.fragment` and `st.container` during fragment reruns. The issue occurs when a fragment contains nested fragments that are rendered inside a container using separate `with container:` context managers. During rerender, the frontend's stale node clearing logic (`ClearStaleNodeVisitor`) appears to incorrectly identify nested fragment elements as stale, causing them to disappear.

The root cause likely lies in how cursor positions and delta paths are restored during fragment reruns combined with how the `fragmentId` and `scriptRunId` are tracked when multiple nested fragments exist within containers. **Bug — `st.data_editor` `NumberColumn` cell commits mid‑IME‑composition.** When a CJK IME is composing in a `NumberColumn` cell editor, the **Enter that confirms the IME composition** (fired with `KeyboardEvent.isComposing === true`) is also treated as "commit cell + move down", so the editor closes after the first digit and multi‑digit entry is impossible. This is the classic IME pitfall — the same class of bug previously fixed for `st.chat_input` in #6988.

**Root cause (candidate):** the cell overlay editor's key handler in the bundled `@glideapps/glide-data-grid` (`internal/data-grid-overlay-editor/…/data-grid-overlay-editor.tsx`, `onKeyDown`) commits on `event.key === "Enter" && !event.shiftKey` **without checking `event.nativeEvent.isComposing`**. Streamlit already has an IME‑safe guard for exactly this (`frontend/lib/src/util/inputUtils.ts` → `isEnterKeyPressed`, which returns `false` when `nativeEvent.isComposing`), but the dataframe/data‑editor overlay path does not go through it. The fix is to add the `isComposing` guard to the overlay editor's Enter/Tab commit.

**Repro confirmed:** with the code sample above, opening a `NumberColumn` cell, composing `1`, then pressing Enter to confirm the composition commits `1` and closes the editor (reproduced here on 1.59.0; the reporter additionally observes it on 1.60.0).

**Note on the regression window:** the bundled `@glideapps/glide-data-grid` version (`6.0.4-alpha24`), `NumberColumn.ts`, and the rendered overlay `<input type="text" inputmode="numeric">` are all **identical** between `1.58.0` and `1.59.0`, and an automated CDP reproduction (dispatching Enter with `isComposing = true`) commits the cell on **both** versions. So the mechanism above is confirmed, but the exact `1.58 → 1.59` behavioral difference the reporter observed could not be isolated via synthetic IME events — it may live in a subtler change among the ~250 commits in that window (focus/re‑render/event‑propagation timing around the overlay) or in a real‑IME nuance the synthetic events don't capture. Recommend verifying with a real macOS CJK IME and, if the version delta matters for the fix, `git bisect 1.58.0..1.59.0` with the provided repro.

### Triage summary

This is a confirmed-looking layout **regression** in the new (`react-aria-components`) `st.selectbox`/ComboBox introduced in 1.59. When a selectbox sits near the bottom of the **sidebar**, its dropdown opens downward and overflows past the viewport instead of flipping up as it did in 1.58.

**Likely root cause:** the dropdown is positioned via Floating UI, but flipping is explicitly disabled inside the sidebar. In `frontend/lib/src/components/shared/Dropdown/Selectbox.tsx` the positioning hook is called with:

```tsx
const { refs, floatingStyles } = useFloatingOverlay({
  open: true,
  placement: "bottom-start",
  offsetPx: convertRemToPx(theme.spacing.twoXS),
  flipOptions: isInSidebar ? false : undefined, // <-- disables flip in the sidebar
  matchTriggerWidth: true,
})
```

In `useFloatingOverlay` (`frontend/lib/src/hooks/useFloatingOverlay.ts`), `flipOptions === false` drops the `flip()` middleware entirely, so the popover can no longer flip to `top` when there isn't enough space below — it just opens downward and gets clipped. This matches the reporter's DOM observation that in 1.59 the listbox renders inside `[data-testid="stSidebar"]` (which is `position: relative`) rather than at the document root as a sibling of `#portal` like in 1.58. This flip-disabling was added in the Floating UI scroll-tracking change (#15638); it was presumably meant to avoid the popover escaping the sidebar's bounds (the BaseWeb `Multiselect` uses the analogous `ignoreBoundary: isInSidebar`), but it also unintentionally removed the upward-flip behavior. A fix likely needs to keep flip enabled while constraining/shifting the popover against the viewport rather than fully disabling `flipOptions` in the sidebar.

- [#12260 – Regression: Selectbox/Multiselect keyboard focus not activating on mobile](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12260): Another regression in the same widgets tied to the `react-aria` ComboBox rewrite — useful as a sibling regression from the same migration.
- [#12865 – Fullscreen menu partially hidden in fixed height containers](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12865): Same class of bug — an overlay/menu getting clipped by a relatively-positioned/overflow-constrained container's bounds instead of being viewport-aware.
- [#9340 – Popover is truncated when app is embedded](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9340): Also an overlay positioning/clipping problem where the popover isn't rendered relative to the viewport; related conceptually rather than a duplicate.

This is a confirmed frontend bug in the `st.expander` (and, via the same shared code path, `st.status`) open/close height animation. After a rapid sequence of expands/collapses, an expander can be left "permanently" clipped — showing a stale fixed height with the tail of its content cut off and unreachable until a rerun/reload replaces the element.

**Root cause (verified against `develop`):** The height animation locks the `<details>` element before animating by setting inline `height: <px>` and `overflow: hidden`, and relies on the Web Animations API `finish` event to clear those inline styles. In `frontend/lib/src/components/elements/Expander/animateHeight.ts`, the `finish` listener clears `element.style.height`/`overflow`, but the `cancel` listener intentionally does **not** (comment: "DON'T clean up on cancel - caller will set new styles"). `cancelAnimation()` in `useDetailsAnimation.ts` likewise only cancels and nulls the ref without clearing styles. This is safe *only if* a cancel is always followed by a new animation that eventually finishes. That assumption breaks when a cancel has no successor — e.g. the debounced `ResizeObserver` callback hits an early-return guard (`!details.open` / `!isOpenRef.current`) or the height delta is under `RESIZE_THRESHOLD_PX` (5px), the deliberate `contentHeight === 0` lock in the open path never gets healed by a ResizeObserver tick, or unmount cleanup. In those cases the inline `height`/`overflow` lock persists, clipping the content. `StyledDetails` in `styled-components.ts` sets no `height`/`overflow` of its own, so any inline `overflow: hidden` observed at rest on the `<details>` is confirmed residue from this cleanup gap. The reporter's analysis and suggested fix (clear inline styles on cancel / in `cancelAnimation()`, since callers already re-lock synchronously) are accurate and align with the code. Marked as a regression since this behavior was introduced with the newer WAAPI-based expander animation (`useDetailsAnimation`, #13933).

I think this could also be a great candidate to [build a custom component](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/components/create) if you're interested in that @Nemecsek!

As an alternative solution I could suggest usage of HTML native, time input field: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/time. 

It has great support (96.87% as of https://caniuse.com/input-datetime) and widget rendering is delegated to the browser. It is also supported by BaseWeb library via `Input` component: https://baseweb.design/components/input/.
